name: Nornir
what_it_is: Nornir is a pure-Python, pluggable multi-threaded automation framework for network devices that lets engineers write and run automation workflows entirely in Python without a DSL. It handles inventory management and concurrent task dispatching across many devices, with an extensible plugin architecture for connections, runners, and inventory backends.
components: Inventory plugins (e.g. nornir-utils SimpleInventory, nornir-napalm, nornir-netbox)
Connection plugins (e.g. nornir-netmiko, nornir-napalm, nornir-scrapli, nornir-paramiko)
Task plugins (user-defined Python functions or community plugins)
protocols: RESTCONF (via nornir-napalm or custom HTTP tasks)
measurement: No built-in metrics collection — timing must be instrumented in custom task code
AggregatedResult and MultiResult objects expose per-host task results and exception details
Failed-host tracking via Result.failed and AggregatedResult.failed_hosts
configuration: config.yaml file for core settings (runner, inventory, logging, ssh)
hosts.yaml for per-device inventory (hostname, port, platform, groups, data)
In-code configuration via InitNornir() kwargs (overrides file-based config)
fault_injection: No native fault-injection primitives — failures are simulated by raising exceptions inside custom task functions
Serial runner can be used to isolate per-device failures without thread-pool interference
modes: ThreadedRunner: parallel execution across hosts with configurable num_workers
SerialRunner: sequential execution, one host at a time
Dry-run behaviour is protocol/plugin-dependent (e.g. NAPALM supports dry-run commits)
constraints: Python 3.10 or higher is required; older Python versions are not supported
No plugins are bundled since v3.0.0 — all connection/inventory plugins must be installed separately via pip
No built-in CLI or REPL; automation logic must be expressed as Python scripts or notebooks
No native Docker image or docker-compose provided in the core repository
Concurrency model is thread-based (GIL-bound), not async/process-based — CPU-heavy tasks do not scale linearly
Inventory data is static at runtime by default; dynamic inventory requires a custom plugin
notable_absences: No docker-compose.yml in the repository (neither master nor main branch)
No built-in protocol implementations — all device communication delegated to connection plugins
No built-in test/assertion framework — test logic must be written in task functions
No built-in secret/credential vault integration (must wire in externally)
No built-in change-rollback mechanism (protocol plugins like NAPALM provide this optionally)
